headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate while the cheatsheet profile is non-executing, making leakage and conflict the main concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP, while agent_b can read/write a Repl workspace but there is no shared channel or ingestion path from agent_a. The pair lacks a direct instruction channel.
conditions: IF agent_a is manually copied into agent_b as text, then injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is added between them, then the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into agent_b.
Use a fixed template for any manual transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read and write Repl workspace files and handles secrets plus deployment config, while agent_a has no file or network surfaces. If both are pointed at the same workspace, agent_b can expose sensitive code or secrets; agent_a itself does not add a second exfiltration path, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same Repl workspace, leakage risk is present.
IF secrets or deployment config are stored in that workspace, exposure impact increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Move secrets out of shared files.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
Review recent file diffs before sharing outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has broad write and git capabilities, but agent_a cannot write files, modify git state, or run code. There is no overlapping mutable capability, so direct conflict is limited to unusual manual coordination rather than default contention.
conditions: IF agent_a is manually used to edit files that agent_b also edits, conflicts can occur.
IF multiple agent_b instances share the same Repl filesystem, write races can occur.
mitigations: Assign only one writer per branch.
Use short-lived branches for agent_b.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Check git status before each handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce reference content that a human may pass to agent_b, and agent_b can act on it with shell, git, and network access. Because agent_b is capable of downstream actions and there is no built-in verification link from agent_a, mistaken or stale content can cascade into incorrect changes.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b as authoritative instructions, cascading errors can propagate.
IF agent_b uses agent_a text without independent verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before actioning text.
Ask agent_b to restate assumptions before executing.
Limit agent_b to read-only review for first pass.
Compare outputs against source docs manually.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification enforcement.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches secrets and deployment configuration and can egress broadly, while agent_a is documentation-only and does not itself process regulated data. The compliance risk is therefore concentrated in agent_b’s handling of sensitive workspace data; agent_a is cited only to show it does not add a second regulated-data surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the Repl workspace, retention and residency controls matter.
IF secrets are stored in files rather than the secrets store, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Store secrets only in the secrets manager.
Review retention settings for the Repl.
Delete temporary files after use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
